arguments.label: Overall account, R001 to R048
arguments.text: Direct response: the supplied records support matched receipt (same tag, full byte count, expected slot, same case) for only 8 of the 48 handoff claims, R001, R007, R013, R019, R025, R031, R037 and R043. Each of those also states a recipient acknowledgment, but that is a separate fact and the receipts are copies from a receiving desk record, not independent observations. The other 40 cases each fail at least one review requirement on the face of the packet: 8 have "not recorded" acknowledgment (R002, R008, R014, R020, R026, R032, R038, R044), 8 carry a tag with an "-earlier" suffix (R003, R009, R015, R021, R027, R033, R039, R045), 8 have an unrecorded destination (R005, R011, R017, R023, R029, R035, R041, R047), 8 differ from the expected byte count by exactly 128 bytes (R004, R010, R016, R022, R028, R034, R040, R046), and 8 carry a receipt header naming another case (R006 says R054, R012 says R060, R018 says R066, R024 says R072, R030 says R078, R036 says R084, R042 says R090, R048 says R096). Of the 8 clean cases, R001, R013, R019, R025, R031, R037 and R043 record an acknowledgment; R007 does too (R007 has no mismatch), so the eight-case clean set is R001, R007, R013, R019, R025, R031, R037 and R043. Limits: the mismatches are on the face of the packets only. They do not prove a failed transfer or a wrong record, since transcription errors or misfiled copies are possible and the packets carry no independent check. Missing acknowledgments and unrecorded destinations are missing evidence, not demonstrated failures. The sender's complete status is not supported for the 40 non-clean cases on these records. Next checks: pull the receiving desk records for each flagged case; for byte gaps, recount at both ends; for case-number and tag mismatches, confirm which bundle the receipt belongs to; for acknowledgments, confirm whether an acceptance record exists.
